issue_context.title: Add slow query statistic information into telemetry data
issue_context.body:
## Development Task
As title, implement this feature.

review_comments: This relies on the implementation of our slow query bucket. I'm not sure whether it is a good idea to set buckets dynamically according to the label from Prometheus query response.
We just dump the bucket and do analysis offline. If the bucket changes, we will just modify our analysis code.
do we need refresh ts to time.Now during retry~?

This ts is used to get the statistic information of slow query bucket from prom. , it won't be so critical to update it when retry. 
Maybe we will miss several slow queries, but it will be count during next report.

how about 

```
	for k := range LastSQBInfo {
		delete(LastSQBInfo, k)
	}
	LastSQBInfo, CurrentSQBInfo = CurrentSQBInfo, LastSQBInfo
```

https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/110055/

Is this more efficient for map generally?

In this case, it should be more efficient.

Accepted.

do we need log error in here, it seems some error didn't have be logged in under method

for example: errors.New("Prom vector expected, got " + value.Type().String())

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/b21aed8cc46e229b74fcd4e96e9f4170ceecde98/telemetry/data_slow_query.go#L89

it seems this error have no chance be logged

I'm not sure whether you should use QueryRange instead of Query (it depends on your requirement. just a note).

For QueryRange: You can query all data points in the time range, so that you can know how this value changes over time.
For Query: You can only query one data point (in this case, last time).
With this case, we just need the latest bucket statistic information, query works well.

I usually met the case where query time.Now() returns nothing, which is caused by either time offsets, or the reporting is not timely. How about using a last-minute ts to hopefully avoid it?

Kai : done.
